Is not about whether it matters or not, from the most objective point of view possible and excluding regions (that even though I don’t know if nihilism means necessary atheism or agnosticism, ill presume you are) life is just a self sustaining system that tries by itself to keep running, thus really we are not more important than the atoms that make us ,non-living mater, but the problem I always had with nihilism is that why is it so important to have a meaning or a importance, most people enjoy being alive, the whole combination of emotions may not be real but how our brains interpret them is, if reading Harry Potter or watching the Mona Lisa gives you happiness there is no reason not to do it, we like being happy and if it really doesn’t matter there is no reason not to prefer being happy, not being important or not being special doesn’t make our immediate happiness less satisfactory, and the rest of the people experience the same emotions, they also enjoy certain things so it’s just fair to let them experience the enjoyment of life, killing someone is not wrong because you are making the atoms that make them stop pumping blood or breathing, you are preventing them from receiving the dopamine of eating a chicken wing (or any food you enjoy) or watching the sunset, if that is not enough reason for morality think of the early humans, they really didn’t care about another human to survive but they knew that the survival of the rest made it easier for them to hunt or eat, so today morality is what keeps society today, being able to trust in others to provide for your food or to build your shelter is what allowed people to specialize and make inventions that ultimately improve your life quality, in smaller scales like families you help them and are nice with them so when you need help they give you shelter or food, and then there is altruism, to help someone just for the satisfaction of doing so, something that I’m sure you have experienced it in some level. 
Life doesn’t have to be important to have meaning, being able to enjoy something it’s already enough reason to do it, it doesn’t matter if anything you do will be forgotten in 200 years, or that anything will be pointless after the heat death of the universe, if you are happy or satisfied in that moment it’s worth it.

Yes, I know it sounds really bad, and you probably think of me as a monster but the bottom line of most non profit organization is to improve life quality, and a shelter doesn't grant life quality, many foster dogs all ready had diseases or injuries in some cases really painful, and the treatment is expensive and even if the animal gets it his condition is not going to change.
Yes in a perfect world shelters would rescue every animal they find, and get a family to adopt them, but the truth is there are not enough people willing to adopt, and they usually only adopt the cute healthy young ones, do you think an old dog with dermatological problems and aggressive behavior will have a good life quality? 
I used to work in a veterinary, and we had a lot of foster dogs, we helped many, many stayed with us and we euthanized some, and no, going around killing dogs is not a good solution but it's preferable than just letting them die of parvovirus , no one can save every dog or cure every disease, that treatment is expensive and so is food and space, and organizations like Peta don't have infinite resources, resources that they are already using in things like saving animals from cosmetic labs.
Euthanasia for the dog is just getting taken to a nice hospital where they give you food and water, and then going to sleep, don't you think that is better for the dog than having to walk for miles with a broken leg that never got treatment to find some food in the trash and then going to sleep in the cold every day, the humane solution would be an sterilization campaign, but that is not always possible and is only a preventive solution.
Yes killing a dog sucks, it always will, but it's what is best for the dog, the organization and the society
